You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Partner Upper-Body Superset Session for 2 lifters
Resource limits: one bench and barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, two ergs, about 25 minutes.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

```json
}
```

This is a Rhylthyme program for a “Partner Upper-Body Superset Session” designed for 2 lifters working as partners against a live clock. The session is intended to take about 25 minutes total, with no wall-clock finishing time specified, so the schedule should finish as early as the work allows. The two people share limited equipment: one flat bench with barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, and two rowing ergs. The core constraint is that each superset has only one of most pieces of equipment available, so the partners must alternate or run opposing exercise stations simultaneously: while one uses the bench, the other uses the dumbbells; while one uses the dumbbells, the other may use the pull-up bar; and both can row at the same time only because there are two ergs. Specific moments matter: warm-up starts together on the ergs, then both do arm circles/band pull-aparts; Superset A uses about 40-second bench and row sets with 90-second rests after both exercises, repeated for 2 rounds; Superset B uses about 45-second dumbbell overhead presses and about 30-second pull-ups, swaps after both are done, rests 2 minutes between rounds but not after the second; cool-down must finish together for 5 minutes of stretching.

The pair must manage singular equipment constraints—one bench/barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, and two ergs—by working opposing stations simultaneously and swapping promptly. Key timed moments include a shared 5-minute rowing warm-up and 3-minute arm/band prep, two rounds of bench press plus dumbbell row with 90-second rests, two rounds of dumbbell overhead press plus pull-ups with no rest after the second, and a shared 5-minute cool-down stretch.",


A track is one sequential line of work: steps inside the same track do not overlap, and any work that happens concurrently belongs in another track. A step has exactly one duration kind: fixed with `seconds`, variable with `minSeconds`/`maxSeconds`/`defaultSeconds`, or indefinite until the person ends it. A `startTrigger` determines when the step begins, using options such as `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. Step IDs are global because triggers may reference steps from any track, so every `stepId` must be unique across the whole program. Each `task` used by a step needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and its `maxConcurrent` controls how many steps can occupy that resource at once, while `actors` records how many people are working. Repeated work should use one step with `replicates` and the appropriate `instances` chain; `maxInFlight` is only for bounded holding areas such as a rack, rotor, or taxiway.

Expected resource constraints for this workout:

- `erg`: maxConcurrent 2; two partners can row simultaneously because there are two ergs.
- `bench_barbell`: maxConcurrent 1; two people are working overall, but only one can use the bench/barbell at a time.
- `dumbbells`: maxConcurrent 1; one pair of dumbbells can be used by only one partner at a time for rows or overhead presses.
- `pullup_bar`: maxConcurrent 1; one pull-up bar can be used by only one partner at a time.
- `bodyweight`: maxConcurrent 2; arm circles, band pull-aparts, rests, and stretching can be done by both partners simultaneously.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; stepIds are global; every task needs a resourceConstraint; repeated work uses replicates/instances/maxInFlight",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "erg", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "bench_barbell", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "dumbbells", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "pullup_bar", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "bodyweight", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or start_workout), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
